recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No follow-up is needed in the current FHIR core branch for FHIR-31526; any future R4B maintenance concern should be handled on the R4B release line.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive BR&R R4B ballot issue requesting that breaking Substance changes be reverted from R4B; comments clarified that the changes were needed for Medication Definition/R5 use cases but should not break R4B compatibility.
initial_application: The Substance changes originated in the FHIR-28547/FHIR-29265/FHIR-29267 family. R4B commits 9f6f0befe9298492d29533eb59378bd0c10eff82 and 6854a80e39c798ffdeee53ca665c5503c28e737f explicitly reverted Substance for FHIR#31526 on the R4B branch, while beb040d0608727a093902f91d4e3d6675f0c33f6 restored the intended Substance model on the main/R5 line.
additional_context: The current combined branch includes active Substance and SubstanceDefinition resources and follows the R5/R6 lineage: Substance.code is a CodeableReference to SubstanceDefinition and expiry/quantity are top-level elements. The origin/R4B branch retains the R4B-compatible CodeableConcept plus Substance.instance/ingredient shape. Later FHIR-48405 cleanup is already represented on the combined branch and confirms that current Substance semantics should not be rolled back to R4B.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reverting the current Substance source to the R4B-compatible shape would undo intentional R5/R6 decisions; FHIR-31526 only required keeping those breaking changes out of R4B, which git history shows was done.
